newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TVNZ 1996 net profit up 40 pct to NZ$60.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: TVNZ 1996 net profit up 40 pct to NZ$60.6 mln.

text.p: New Zealand television network Television New Zealand (TVNZ) on Wednesday reported a 40 percent rise in 1996 net profit to a record NZ$60.6 million.
Operating profit was $87.2 million, up $20.4 million on 1995, based on a $30.5 million lift in revenue to $458 million.
Dividends to the government totalled $62.4 million, including a special dividend of $20 million.

"Of the $30.5 million revenue increase, only $4.4 million (14.5 percent) came from advertising revenue, reflecting a difficult advertising market last year, but nearly $26.1 million (85.5 percent) came from other revenue," TVNZ said.
Total advertising revenue was $293 million and other revenue was $165 million, up 3.5 percent.
Group Chief Executive Chris Anderson said he was pleased with the result.

However, he warned the that market was increasingly tough, reflecting a soft advertising outlook, some uncertainty over government broadcasting policies and increased competition in the free-to-air market.
